title_en: Notice of the Supreme People's Court on the Application of the Provisions on Time Limits for Adducing Evidence in the Several Provisions on Evidence in Civil Proceedings
full_text_en:
Supreme People's Court

Notice on the Application of the Relevant Provisions on the Time Limit for Producing Evidence in the "Several Provisions on Evidence in Civil Litigation"

Fa Fa [2008] No. 42

To all local people's courts at various levels, all military courts, all railway transport intermediate courts and basic courts, all maritime courts, and people's courts at various levels of the Xinjiang Production and Construction Corps:

Since the implementation of the "Several Provisions on Evidence in Civil Litigation" (hereinafter referred to as the "Evidence Provisions") of the Supreme People's Court on April 1, 2002, it has played a positive role in guiding and regulating the trial activities of people's courts, enhancing the evidentiary awareness of litigants, and promoting the fair and orderly conduct of civil trial activities. However, with the emergence of new circumstances and new issues, some localities have inconsistent understandings of certain individual provisions in the "Evidence Provisions," particularly the provisions concerning the time limit for producing evidence. In order to effectively ensure the full exercise of litigants' procedural rights and ensure the fair and efficient exercise of adjudicative power by people's courts, the following notice is hereby given on the application of the provisions on the time limit for producing evidence in the "Evidence Provisions" and related matters:

I. Concerning the issue of the time limit for producing evidence as provided in Article 33, Paragraph 3. The time limit for producing evidence as provided in Article 33, Paragraph 3 of the "Evidence Provisions" refers to the period during which, when applying ordinary first-instance procedures to hear civil cases, the people's court designates for the parties to provide evidence to prove the basic facts supporting their claims. This period shall not be less than thirty days. However, if the people's court obtains the consent of both parties, the designated time limit for producing evidence may be less than thirty days. After the expiration of the aforementioned time limit for producing evidence, for a specific fact, specific evidence, or based on specific reasons, the people's court may, according to the specific circumstances of the case, discretionarily designate a time limit for the parties to provide evidence or rebuttal evidence. This time limit is not subject to the restriction of "not less than thirty days."

II. Concerning the issue of the time limit for producing evidence in cases tried under summary procedures. For cases tried under summary procedures, the time limit for producing evidence designated by the people's court is not subject to the restriction of Article 33, Paragraph 3 of the "Evidence Provisions" and may be less than thirty days. Where summary procedures are converted to ordinary procedures for trial, if the time limit for producing evidence designated by the people's court is less than thirty days, the people's court shall supplement the parties with a time limit for producing evidence of not less than thirty days. However, with the consent of the parties, the time limit for producing evidence designated by the people's court may be less than thirty days.

III. Concerning the issue of the time limit for producing evidence after a party raises an objection to jurisdiction. If a party raises an objection to jurisdiction during the first-instance defense period, the people's court shall, after the ruling rejecting the party's objection to jurisdiction becomes effective, re-designate a time limit for producing evidence of not less than thirty days in accordance with Article 33, Paragraph 3 of the "Evidence Provisions." However, with the consent of the parties, the people's court may designate a time limit for producing evidence of less than thirty days.

IV. Concerning the issue of the time limit for producing evidence to rebut evidence collected by the people's court ex officio. Where the people's court collects evidence ex officio in accordance with Article 15 of the "Evidence Provisions" and it is presented at trial, and a party requests to provide rebuttal evidence, the people's court may discretionarily determine an appropriate time limit for producing evidence.

V. Concerning the issue of the time limit for producing evidence when additional parties are added. Where the people's court adds a party or a third party with an independent claim to participate in the litigation, it shall, in accordance with Article 33, Paragraph 3 of the "Evidence Provisions," designate a time limit for producing evidence for the newly added litigant. This time limit for producing evidence shall apply to the other parties as well.

VI. Concerning the issue of a party's application to extend the time limit for producing evidence. If a party's application to extend the time limit for producing evidence is granted by the people's court, in order to equally protect the procedural rights of both parties, the extended time limit for producing evidence shall apply to the other parties.

VII. Concerning the issue of the time limit for producing evidence when increasing or changing claims or filing a counterclaim. Where a party increases or changes its claims or files a counterclaim within the first-instance time limit for producing evidence, or where, after the people's court informs the parties that they may change their claims in accordance with Article 35 of the "Evidence Provisions," the parties change their claims, the people's court shall re-designate a time limit for producing evidence based on the specific circumstances of the case. If the parties have agreed on a time limit for producing evidence, the matter shall be handled in accordance with Article 33, Paragraph 2 of the "Evidence Provisions."

VIII. Concerning the issue of the time limit for producing evidence for new evidence in second instance. During the trial by the second instance people's court, if a party applies to provide new evidence, the time limit for producing evidence designated by the people's court is not subject to the restriction of "not less than thirty days."

IX. Concerning the issue of the time limit for producing evidence in cases remanded for retrial. For cases remanded for retrial, when the first instance people's court conducts a new trial, it may, taking into account the specific circumstances of the case and the reasons for the remand, discretionarily determine the time limit for producing evidence. If the case was remanded due to a violation of legal procedures, the people's court, after soliciting the opinions of the parties, may no longer designate a time limit for producing evidence or may discretionarily designate a time limit for producing evidence. However, if the case was remanded due to the omission of a party, the matter shall be handled in accordance with Article 5 of this Notice. If the case was remanded due to unclear findings of fact or insufficient evidence, the people's court may require the parties to negotiate and determine a time limit for producing evidence, or may discretionarily designate a time limit for producing evidence. The aforementioned time limits for producing evidence are not subject to the restriction of "not less than thirty days."

X. Concerning the issue of determining new evidence. When determining "new evidence," the people's court shall, in accordance with Articles 41, 42, 43, and 44 of the "Evidence Provisions," comprehensively determine it by considering the following factors:

(1) Whether the evidence objectively existed within the time limit for producing evidence or within other time limits specified in Articles 41 and 44 of the "Evidence Provisions";

(2) Whether the party's failure to provide evidence within the time limit for producing evidence or within other time limits specified in the judicial interpretation was due to intentional conduct or gross negligence.

December 11, 2008
